title.narrative: Climate and Disaster Resilience Enhancement Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The proposed program will support the enhancement of Pakistan's resilience to disasters triggered by natural hazards and the impacts of climate change. Through an integrated approach, the program will support (i) strengthened institutional capacity for strategy, planning, and response; (ii) increased investment in disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate resilience; and (iii) enhanced disaster risk financing (DRF) using a risk-layered approach. A policy-based loan (PBL) is appropriate given the need for evidence-based policy dialogue, effective stakeholder consultation, and well-coordinated development partner support. The programmatic approach comprising two subprograms is adopted to sequence complex and strategic reforms across multiple implementing agencies, policies, and plans. Subprogram 1 will be a PBL, and subprogram 2 will be a PBL with a contingent disaster financing (CDF) option. This is ADB's first use of CDF using a PBL programmatic approach and the first CDF in the Central and West Asia Region.

Reports and Recommendations of the President

2.1. To enhance the climate resilience of government infrastructure, the Planning Commission published climate-related requirements in the Manual of Development Projects and proformas for public sector investments and issued accompanying guidelines for conducting climate change risk management and greenhouse gas reduction assessments.

2.2. To increase the scale and efficiency of mobilizing and catalyzing climate and disaster risk reduction investments, the NDRMF Board approved the gender-responsive NDRMF Business Strategy 2023–2033 with a 3-year investment plan and commenced implementation by establishing a project preparation facility (PPF).q

2.3. To increase mobilization of international climate finance in Pakistan, the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MOCC&EC): i. Notified the establishment of the Climate Change Authority in line with the Climate Change Act, 2017 and commenced recruitment of staff. ii. Established a climate finance wing at MOCC&EC, staffed with professionals performing roles related to facilitating and reporting on the mobilization of climate finance; and initiated preparation of the National Climate Finance Strategy (NCFS). iii. Institutionalized and operationalized an online dashboard for monitoring the mobilization of international climate finance.

2.4. To advance Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG)-compliant investments in climate and disaster resilient infrastructure: i. The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) approved the gender-sensitive Guidelines on ESG Disclosures for Listed Companies, 2023 and facilitated issuance of an ESG primer outlining ESG best practices at the Pakistan Stock Exchange. ii. MOF issued a road map for the issuance of an inaugural listed domestic sovereign green sukuk for mobilizing capital to sustainable resilience investments.

3.1. To establish a coherent risk-layered framework for scaling up DRF instruments, the NDRMF Board approved the DRF Strategy of Pakistan and an associated road map. MOF commenced the implementation of the strategy by allocating an initial Pakistan rupee (PRs)15 billion contingent budgetary allocation for disasters triggered by natural hazards in the fiscal year (FY) 2024–2025 budget.

3.2. To facilitate timely and equitable cash transfers in the event of a disaster, especially for female-headed families, BISP: i. Launched a dynamic registry of households that captures changing circumstances following external shocks. ii. Issued a methodology for identifying and targeting families in urgent need of financial assistance in response to a disaster. iii. Broadened the accessibility of the dynamic registry by expanding biometric verification-based payment touchpoints to all Union Councils.
